The maximum is $k = 14$. The upper bound is proved below, but I did not construct an explicit placement that reaches it, so attainment rests on a plausibility check and my recollection of the known answer.

**Reading the condition.** A rook attacks the first rook it sees along its row or column in each direction. So "each rook attacks only rooks of the opposite color" means that, in every row and every column, the rooks in order along the line must alternate in color.

**Upper bound.** In a line with $b$ black and $w$ white rooks that alternate in color, $|w-b|\le 1$, so $w\le b+1$. Summing over the 8 rows gives
$$k \le \sum_{\text{rows}} (b_i+1) = 6+8 = 14.$$

**Attainability (not verified).** Equality needs every row and every column to have exactly one more white rook than black. Such a placement has 6 black and 14 white rooks. I did not build one explicitly. I tried a few partial patterns, such as a 3×3 checkerboard patch, which fails because its middle row has more black than white. I settled on 14 as the known answer, with the bound above showing it cannot be exceeded.

ANSWER: 14
